# Panel review — routing ladder, sweep, and readiness (single-shot)

Baseline first: in this copy the suite is **4,793 passed, 2 failed, 4 skipped** (14:48). Both failures are artefacts of reviewing a copy, not regressions: `test_the_sandbox_flag_distinguishes_the_two_cases` asserts `.git` is a *directory* (here it is a 91-byte worktree pointer file), and the ledger drift test fails because the 12 empty aborted-run directories don't survive copying, so the regenerated ledger loses one line. Your 4,799/0 claim is substantively confirmed — but note anyone replicating from a tarball or worktree will see a red suite.

## Q1. Why the ladder exhausts where one sweep dispatch succeeds

I re-executed both paths' mechanics against the run artefacts. The premise dissolves under that: **the sweep did not out-falsify the ladder — the ladder had already falsified every distinct defect in the queue, and the sweep's "27 cleared" is largely bookkeeping corruption.** The chain, each link tool-checked:

**1. The 16-finding registry contains ~4 distinct defects.** The final falsifier bodies come in exactly three byte-identical groups of five — {C0001,C0004,C0007,C0011,C0013} (reingest guard), {C0002,C0005,C0008,C0010,C0014} (pi_mem denominator), {C0003,C0006,C0009,C0012,C0015} (`_check_count` bound) — plus C0016 (CUSUM). Six seats each reported the same plants; nothing upstream merged them.

**2. "Full routing ladder exhausted" means "2 of 5 asked."** `route()` defaults `max_rungs=2` and `_apply_routing` never overrides it (routing.py:206, no caller argument). With the source seat excluded, the rungs actually reached were only Codex/CC2/ChatGPT — the dispatch ledger shows **DeepSeek-SIM received zero routing dispatches**, which is by charter: it is ranked last and, at 2 rungs on a 6-seat panel, unreachable at any severity. The `hil_reason` text overstates by three models.

**3. Every "irreducible" critical was a duplicate of a defect the ladder itself confirmed the same round.** C0001/C0004/C0013 restate the guard defect Codex confirmed as C0011; C0014 restates the pi_mem defect Codex confirmed as C0002/C0005/C0010. The ladder resolved 7 of 11 routed findings — covering all three plant groups — then locked rewordings of its own successes as irreducible. Nothing genuinely hard was in the queue.

**4. Why the ladder's own dedup guard ("a duplicate of a confirmed defect must never reach HIL") failed, twice over.** (a) The 0.85 word-overlap bar is unreachable for cross-model rewordings: I measured C0001↔C0011 = 0.179, C0013↔C0011 = 0.157, C0014↔C0002 = 0.238. That threshold catches near-verbatim restatements (the Exp-42 case) and nothing else. (b) Latent second bug: the `confirmed` snapshot is built **once, before the loop** (:4840–4844), so same-round routing confirms are invisible to later items regardless of threshold.

**5. The sweep's "success" decomposes into three defects I reproduced with stubs against the real `_post_convergence_sweep`:**

- **The settle is gated `if converged:` (:12538) on a halt path.** Its comment says "Runs unconditionally"; the sweep's docstring says settle "runs immediately before this"; a shipped test (`test_the_call_is_reachable_and_guarded_only_by_convergence`) pins the gate. When the sweep was widened to run on halts (2026-08-01), the settle wasn't — so on every halted run, findings the ladder already CONFIRMED+verified (7 here) are re-offered to the panel as "residuals."
- **Re-clear + count inflation.** CONFIRMED ∉ `_TERMINAL`, the prompt is built once before the model loop, and the `finditer` loop never checks `_handled`. My repro: one finding, one reply with two labelled blocks → `cleared: 2`, `reverify` executed twice (model code run twice). Hence **`cleared: 27` on a 16-entry registry**.
- **Attribution overwrite.** Second repro: model A clears C0001; model B's reply (built from the pre-loop prompt listing everything) re-clears it → `items.by` and `resolved_by_sweep` both read model B. So **"all 27 by DeepSeek-SIM" is unreliable**: CC2-SIM's 16,051-char sweep reply (dispatched first, before DeepSeek's 10,378) may have cleared up to 11 of them and had the credit stolen. Which model cleared what is unrecoverable — sweep replies are persisted nowhere.

**6. The real prompt/context differences, for completeness.** Same decider both paths (`reverify_falsifier`; both default to `REPO_ROOT` — though `route()` calls it *without* `repo_root` while the sweep passes it through, an inert trap today). The material asymmetry: for a **python** target the ladder rung prompt contains *no target source at all* ("read the real code via inspect"), while the sweep pastes the full seeded 20,605-byte module verbatim, plus all sibling residual descriptions — a model shown four rewordings of the same line plus the line itself has almost nothing left to do. (The ladder's *prose* branch already pastes the source; the python branch is the odd one out.) Also: ladder desc[:1200] solo vs sweep desc[:400] batched; and sweep clears skip the discrimination control that in-round confirms face (:4290–4330) — the sweep is the *weakest* verification gate in the system, and it accepted the identical falsifier body for five different finding ids.

**7. Two more ladder defects, verified:** the alarm's evidence bundle attaches `routing_history` per item (:5567) — **written nowhere in the codebase**, empty in every archived alarm across three runs; and `RoutingResult.last_code`/`last_verdict` are dropped on the HIL path. That is why "why exactly did CC2/ChatGPT fail on C0013/C0014" cannot be answered from the artefact — I checked and I could not; labelled unchecked. And "LOCK" is not a lock: my repro shows an irreducible-stamped critical is re-dispatched to the same two rungs every subsequent round — on a real run with a within-bound queue, paid dispatch to already-failed writers indefinitely, exactly the "endlessly re-ask" routing.py's docstring forswears.

**Verdict on your dichotomy:** the exhaustion criterion is too eager (2 rungs, wrong wording, no audit trail), and the sweep does one thing worth adopting — paste the target source into the python rung prompt. But the binding failure is upstream: **cross-model duplicate handling**. Fix that and this queue is empty before the alarm looks. Note also exp55: on real vendors the sweep cleared **0 of 8** — the rescue you're asking about does not generalize; it was a property of this run's duplicates-plus-settle-bug, not of one more dispatch.

## Q2. Should the sweep run before the alarm?

**No.** Three grounds. (1) This run is the existence proof of the current order's value: the alarm caught a real mechanical failure (dedup + ladder truncation) that a pre-verdict sweep would have laundered into a clean convergence — and the "rescue" it would have laundered with is one I've shown to be part settle-bug, part duplicate-clearing, verified at a lower bar (no discrimination control), with corrupted counts and attribution. (2) On the only real-vendor data (exp55 ×2) the sweep rescues nothing, so moving it buys no robustness where money is spent. (3) The non-rescuing property is load-bearing for the paper: a sweep that can pre-empt the alarm is a convergence input, and every one of its defects becomes verdict-affecting.

Do instead, in order: ungate the settle so code matches its own comment (halts included — that alone removes the "sweep re-clears confirmed findings" spectacle); add `_handled` to the finditer loop and build the prompt per-model from `live`; make ladder exhaustion mean the panel (config `max_rungs`, default all non-source seats); persist per-rung and per-sweep replies and verdicts (populate `routing_history`; seal them in the chain — today the chain seals only the 6 round-0 replies and the report, so the decisive dispatches of a falsification methodology are off the record); and give the irreducible census a duplicate annotation so a human opening the bundle sees "3 items, 2 defects." The alarm stays exactly where it is and, per your constraint, the bound stays at 2 — with dedup fixed, this queue would have been 0, not 3.

## Verify-or-refute

**1. id-reuse threshold 0.20 — partially holds; two measured failure modes.** Symmetric rewordings absorb correctly (0.33–1.0), and empty signatures fail toward absorption as designed. But (a) *your exact worry is real*: a terse-vs-verbose genuine repeat scores 0.07–0.18 (numbers — line numbers, dates, severities — dilute the union), gets double-registered, and the double-registration reaches conviction: it feeds the settled novelty series that overwrites `novel_critical_history[-1]`, resets the K-zero streak, and depresses `_estimate_gamma` — convergence-delaying, i.e. money-burning, not result-faking. (b) Worse and unflagged in your brief: **every constructed same-file/same-function different-defect pair scored ≥ 0.20 — two at exactly 1.0** (signatures reduce to `{record_experiment, exp_id}`-style location tokens; I reproduced 1.0 with my own pair). The original finding-deletion bug survives for precisely the most probable id-reuse case, and the shipped test covers only a cross-file pair sharing zero tokens. The threshold was calibrated on unlocated findings; you are applying it to pairs that by construction share a location — the population where location tokens maximally collide. Compare falsifier/fix fields too, or exclude location tokens from this particular comparison.

**2. Mutants — your four kills verified; seven survivors demonstrated.** min→max, `>=`, `too_new=False`, `>newest+1` all die; the commissioning tests do what they claim. But the surviving surface is wide (each survivor demonstrated by `--json` diff, several corroborated by my own exec-shim runs): **M13** `elif w["gated"]:` → `elif not w["gated"]:` flips 16 of 51 verdicts including every AMBIGUOUS/UNREACHABLE — the tool's self-described "actionable" verdict is entirely unpinned; **M06** live `newest = max(...)` → `min(...)` silently kills the age control on the live path (every test pins via `--as-of`); **M10** witness radius 40→4; **M11** `counts[other] > 0` → `>= 0` (unwitnessed siblings count as witnesses); **M12** single-sighting keys unprotected; **M07** report-shape disjunct loosely constrained; **M15** `lines` field untested. Incidental: the sibling picker iterates a set (nondeterministic across runs), and **`CONFIG_ALIASES` is never applied** — the docstring's "alias resolution" design constraint is echoed into output and enforced by nothing.

**3. `_is_simulated_report` — current verdicts all correct, safety circumstantial.** All 15 exclusions genuine, none of the 73 kept reports simulated, and the three-key TOO_NEW reversion reproduces under the pinned baseline. But: your "82→73" is stale (85→73 at the landing commit, 88→73 now); false exclusion is demonstrable three ways (body-rule on quoted sim names — 7 real panel files already trip it, one with first `-SIM` at char 3,924 of the 4,000 window; dir substrings `_simple`/`similarity…`; case-sensitivity is silently load-bearing); false inclusion two ways (long-header sim report; `simulated_bench_last.json` at logs root, whose *filename* is never checked). The body rule is currently unfalsifiable dead weight — every sim report is already dir-excluded. And the mtime age baseline disarms TOO_NEW in any fresh checkout. Key on an explicit provenance field (`models` ending `-SIM`, or a runner-written `simulated: true`), not directory spelling.

**4. Case-normalisation — holds.** Exhaustive sweep found no genuinely distinct identities differing only by case anywhere; the sole consumer is `distinct_models` (dispatch uses `mc.model_id` verbatim); the error direction of a hypothetical collision is conservative (fewer distinct challengers → harder refutation); 109 covering tests pass.

**5. Canary v2 — real improvement, and the flattery partially moved.** MEM2-CUSUM **is** findable without the key, by three independent in-file routes — decisively, seeding makes lines 335–336 token-identical updates, so "two-sided" is provably vacuous by code logic alone; also the surviving docstring/comment, and the header's replay figure "trough CUSUM− −0.500," impossible under `max(0.0,·)`. Split balance is nominally real (each split ≥1 easy + 1 hard) and held-out p̂ now discriminates seats (Codex 1.0 vs 0.667) — genuine progress over v1's uniform 1.000. But: **MEM2-REINGEST fails C1's letter** (the Raises-contract states the invariant adjacently; caught 5/5, behaviourally an easy control, labelled medium); **MEM2-CUSUM fails C2's purpose** (the header declares the drift subsystem UNREACHED — the exact argue-the-panel-out-of-the-site mechanism C2 was written against; 4/5 seats missed it); the run's docstring-citation rate *rose* to 16/16 (v1: 17/22); the only plant with no adjacent prose (RESET) was the one 0/5 missed — **and it sits in calibration, the split the headline p̂ refuses to score**; and v1's own disqualifying standard (seed alone, run the module's test suite) was silently dropped from the criteria — measured: the three caught plants fail 3–4 tests each, both hard plants pass 84/84. Either that standard was wrong then or v2 is unfair now; the closure notes currently claim both. (Also: "MEM2-REINGEST, 4 separate entries" in the runway note — the registry has 5.)

## Q3. Ready for a real experiment?

**Not yet — and one premise needs correcting first: v3 has already met real vendors.** The exp55 twin control runs (2026-08-23, CC2/ChatGPT/Codex/DeepSeek/Gemini, no `-SIM`) carry the v3-only alarm-evidence schema; both halted on `HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM` at round ≤1, alarm count 7 vs bound 2, sweep clearing 0. Combined with this run: every v3 outing against a defect-bearing or prose target that reached the alarm has halted the same way, and **no real run under v3 has ever converged**. The failure mode you'd be paying to hit again is already characterized: N seats find the same defects, dedup can't merge rewordings, ≥3 of the restatements fail their falsifiers, ladder asks 2 writers, alarm trips. On a real 6-seat panel this is close to guaranteed on any target with a few genuine criticals.

Before spending money, in priority order — none of this is currently checked by any test (the 104 routing/sweep/settle tests all pass over every defect above):

1. **Duplicate handling before the alarm census** (Q1/Q2 above). This is the it-halts-again item.
2. **The sweep bookkeeping cluster** — settle gate, `_handled`, per-model prompts, attribution. This run's report of record already misstates counts and credit, and your brief repeated both as fact; that is evidentiary material for a paper.
3. **Persistence** — rung and sweep replies into the sealed chain; populate `routing_history`. You could not answer your own Q1 from the artefact, and neither could I.
4. **The same-location id-reuse absorption** (item 1b). My candidate for "most likely to be wrong in a way nobody has noticed": it deletes real findings silently, in the most common reuse scenario, behind a fix that was shipped *as* finding-preservation, with a test that exercises only the pair shape that cannot collide.
5. **Sweep clears through the discrimination control**, same bar as in-round confirms — identical code accepted for five ids in this run is exactly what that control exists to interrogate.
6. Smaller: `max_rungs` configurable; re-routing of "locked" items bounded; `reverify` repo_root asymmetry closed; sim-filter provenance field; audit-tool survivors (M13, M06); the two environment-fragile tests; cost model — this one-round sim burned 24 real dispatches / ~46 minutes wall on a 489-line target, and PRIVATE_NOTES says resources are tight; and the directive-asymmetry confound in PRIVATE_NOTES remains open for between-model claims.

**Unchecked, stated plainly:** why CC2/ChatGPT's specific rung replies for C0013/C0014 produced nothing confirmable (unpersisted — unknowable); which sweep model actually cleared which residual (overwritten — unknowable); why C0004 carried the irreducible stamp but escaped the alarm census of 3 (a consistent CONTESTED→CONFIRMED explanation exists; not verified); and the out-of-tree catalogue contents I relied on my sub-reviewer's executed evidence for rather than re-deriving independently.

The alarm was right, both times you defended it and here. It is the only instrument in this system that has never lied to you — the ladder's `hil_reason`, the sweep's `cleared`, the sweep's `by`, and the settle's comment all have. Fix the things that lied; leave the thing that didn't exactly where it is.
